concepts.why: The patient presented with binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze and inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline, which are characteristic symptoms of abducens nerve palsy, confirmed by the presence of left-sided abducens nerve palsy immediately following surgery.
The patient's symptoms of bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, and facial pain and pressure, which were recalcitrant to multiple treatments, are consistent with chronic rhinosinusitis.

The patient developed left-sided abducens nerve palsy immediately following surgery, which resolved by postoperative day 1, suggesting a complication related to the sphenopalatine ganglion blockade procedure.

It explains the normal intraocular pressure measurements and low National Institutes of Health stroke score despite the presence of abducens nerve palsy, which could be caused by a cavernous sinus thrombosis.
